newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign investors drive up Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors drive up Delhi shares.

text.p: Delhi shares opened higher in hectic trade on Thursday, propelled by foreign investors' buying, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was up 2.02 points at 859.97 after 30 minutes of trade.
"It seems that the market has been mainly driven by foreign institutional investors, centred around some particular counters," said Deepak Asrani of brokers R.B. Financial Consultants.
Reliance Industries Ltd traded 1.20 rupees higher at 321.25.
State Bank of India, which was due to announce its 1996/97 (April-March) results later on Thursday, rose one rupee to 325.50.
ACC shares fell 7.85 rupees to 1,162 after the firm on Wednesday announced a sharp decline in 1996/97 net profit to 769.2 million rupees from 2.27 billion in the previous financial year.
